;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Use of chemical weapons in the Syrian Civil War]]
**The [[United Nations]] [[United Nations Security Council|Security Council]] meets amid concerns of military strikes in [[Syria]] by the [[United States]] and its allies following [[Douma chemical attack|a suspected chemical weapons attack]] in Syria last weekend, with the United States ambassador to the UN, [[Nikki Haley]], accusing [[Russia]] of lies and covering for the government of [[President of Syria|Syrian President]] [[Bashar al-Assad]], which she said had used chemical weapons at least 50 times in the past [[Syrian Civil War|seven years of warfare]], and the Russian ambassador to the UN, [[Vassily Nebenzia]], blaming the United States, [[France]] and [[United Kingdom|the UK]] for escalating tensions. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/national-security/as-un-security-council-meets-on-syria-haley-accuses-russia-of-lies-and-a-coverup/2018/04/13/e2853e46-3f21-11e8-974f-aacd97698cef_story.html?noredirect=on (''The Washington Post'')]
**The [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] issues a statement saying it is "highly likely" the Assad regime used chemical weapons on its own people, and that since such an action could not go unchallenged, Britain would work with United States and France to coordinate an international response, without specifying what measures the United Kingdom would take. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/04/12/middleeast/uk-france-support-us-syria-airstrikes-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**Protests enter a third week, with thousands taking part. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/1000s-of-palestinians-demonstrate-at-gaza-border-for-a-3rd-week-hundreds-injured/2018/04/13/04bfa6d8-3db3-11e8-955b-7d2e19b79966_story.html?noredirect=on (''The Washington Post'')]
**The [[Israeli Defence Forces]] claim an [[improvised explosive device]] was set off near the [[Israel–Gaza border|Gazan border]] with possible [[State of Palestine|Palestinian]] casualties and other protestors attempted unsuccessfully to fly a kite carrying a firebomb over the border fence. [http://www.jpost.com/Breaking-News/Protesters-set-off-explosive-try-to-fly-kite-bomb-over-border-549740 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
**Israel opens fire again, with the [[Gaza Health Ministry]] claiming one [[Palestinian people|Palestinian]] was killed and 233 injured as protesters torched tyres and [[Flag of Israel|Israeli flags]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/gaza-protests-dozens-of-palestinians-wounded-by-israeli-fire-reports-say-1.5994845 (''Haaretz'')]
**The [[International Federation of Journalists]], [[Norwegian Refugee Council]], and [[Committee to Protect Journalists]] criticise Israeli authorities for shooting dead [[Yaser Murtaja]] during his coverage of the protests last week. The IFJ calls Murtaja's death murder and its general secretary accuses Israel of "fabricating lies" to support the killing. [http://www.jpost.com/Arab-Israeli-Conflict/Terrorist-or-journalist-Who-really-was-the-slain-Gazan-Yaser-Murtaja-549709 (''The Jeruslalem Post'')]
*Police say a bombing took place in [[Barawe]], [[Lower Shabelle]], [[Somalia]], at a [[Association football|football]] stadium yesterday, the first time a stadium in the country has been targeted, killed up to five spectators. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-security/bomb-kills-up-to-five-during-football-match-in-somalia-idUSKBN1HK0EY (Reuters)]
*Armed bandits storm a mining site in the northwestern [[Nigeria]]n state of [[Zamfara]], killing 26 people, including 16 illegal gold miners. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/04/13/africa/nigerias-zamfara-killings-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*The Government of [[Ecuador]] says that the three Ecuadorian journalists kidnapped by rebel members of the [[Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia]] on 26 March have been murdered. President [[Lenín Moreno]] orders military operations on the Colombian border to catch the murderers, offering a reward of US$100,000. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/13/ecuador-colombia-journalists-military-strike-rebels (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Poisoning of Yulia and Sergei Skripal]]
**Sir [[Mark Sedwill]], [[national security]] advisor to the [[United Kingdom]], says [[Russia]]n intelligence targeted [[Yulia Skripal]]'s email account. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-43755789 (BBC)]

;Disasters and accidents 
*[[List of shipwrecks in 2018|Shipwrecks in 2018]]
**The fire aboard [[Korean Peninsula|Korea]]n ship FV ''Dong Won 701'' in the [[Timaru|Port of Timaru]], [[New Zealand]], enters its fifth day. [[Fire and Emergency New Zealand]] rejects a proposal to tow the vessel out to sea as too dangerous. Firefighters commence efforts to seal the ship to suffocate ongoing fires. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/timaru-herald/news/103076156/two-fires-possibly-still-burning-on-korean-fishing-boat-in-timaru (Stuff)]
*A bus overturns near the village of [[Vakarel]], [[Bulgaria]], killing six people and injuring 20. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bulgaria-crash/bus-crash-near-bulgarian-capital-kills-six-and-injures-more-than-20-idUSKBN1HK1G4 (Reuters)]
*[[Vanuatu]] plans another evacuation from [[Ambae Island]] due to volcanic activity from [[Manaro Voui]]. [https://www.radionz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/354953/vanuatu-govt-plans-another-evacuation-from-ambae (RNZ)]
*[[Summit Air Flight 409]]
**The [[Nepal]]ese Accident Investigation Commission concludes its investigation, finding the plane [[aerodynamic stall|stalled]] after the flight crew lost situational awareness and began a rapid ascent to avoid terrain whilst still configured for landing. [http://avherald.com/h?article=4a9877a9&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)]
*[[Russia]]n authorities say a [[Kamov Ka-29]] belonging to the [[Baltic Fleet]] crashed late yesterday whilst attempting to land on a ship, killing two people. [https://www.rferl.org/a/two-die-in-russian-navy-helicopter-crash/29165721.html (RadioFreeEurope / Radio Liberty)]

;Health and environment
*The [[International Maritime Organisation]] announces agreements to reduce shipping emissions by 50% of 2008 levels by 2050, and to ban [[heavy fuel oil]] from the [[Arctic]]. [http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/international-shipping-emissions-cut-1.4618829 (CBC)] [https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-imo-emissions/u-n-shipping-agency-reaches-deal-to-cut-co2-emissions-idUKKBN1HK20F (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Terrorism in France]]
**[[France|French]] judges clear the [[Tarnac Nine]], accused of  performing an [[anarchist terrorism|anarchist]] terror sabotage in a controversial trial, of wrongdoing and describe the existence of a terror group as a "fiction". Defence lawyers had accused ex-[[president of France|President]] [[Nicolas Sarkozy]]'s government of misusing counterterror law. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/13/tarnac-nine-leftwing-anarchist-terror-cell-fiction-france (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Terrorism in Germany]]
**Three [[Syria]]n nationals are arrested in [[Saarland]] suspected of terror links. Two are suspected of fighting with [[ISIL|the Islamic State]] in Syria. [http://www.dw.com/en/german-police-arrest-three-terror-suspects/a-43372746 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Right-wing terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**An unidentified civilian is jailed for three and a half years for [[terrorism Acts|terror offences]] connected to banned [[neo-Nazi]] group [[National Action (UK)|National Action]]. Acquitted [[Finland|Finnish]] national Mikko Vehvilainen, a serving soldier in the British Army, is jailed alongside him for a weapons offence, receiving 12 months. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-43747111 (BBC)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-mid-wales-43756623 (BBC)] [https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/soldier-accused-recruiting-national-action-14411187 (''The Birmingham Mail'')]
*[[LGBT rights in Portugal]]
**The [[Parliament of Portugal]] passed a new law, by a 109 vote margin, making it easier for people to change their legal gender. [[Portugal|Portuguese]] citizens from the age of 16 will now be able to change their gender and name in documents without the need of a medical report. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-43740417 (BBC)]
*[[First presidency of Donald Trump|Presidency of Donald Trump]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] [[List of people granted executive clemency in the first presidency of Donald Trump|pardons]] former [[Vice President of the United States|Vice-President]] [[Dick Cheney]]'s [[Chief of Staff to the Vice President of the United States|Chief of Staff]] [[Lewis "Scooter" Libby]], who was convicted of lying about leaks to the media. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-43747229 (BBC)]
*[[2016 Ludwigshafen bombing plot]]
**An [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] member is sentenced in [[Vienna]] to nine years in prison, among others for instigating a 12-year-old boy to commit a Christmas market bombing in Ludwigshafen, Germany. [http://www.dw.com/en/vienna-court-imprisons-teen-over-planned-christmas-attacks-in-germany/a-43383844 (Deutsche Welle)]
*An [[improvised explosive device]] goes off prematurely in Wardaka, [[Baghlan]], [[Afghanistan]], killing nine insurgents and injuring five more. [https://www.tolonews.com/afghanistan/nine-insurgents-killed-own-ied-explosion (Tolo News)]
*[[Terrorism in Iraq]]
**[[ISIL|Islamic State]] claim responsibility for bomb attacks on [[al-Hashd al-Shaabi]] in [[Asdeira]], [[Saladin Governorate|Salahuddin]], [[Iraq]] that killed at least ten. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/islamic-state-claims-responsibility-killing-injuring-tens-of-people-in-blasts-north-of-salahuddin/ (Iraqi News)]
**The [[Iraq]]i [[Interior Ministry]] announces the arrest of six alleged [[ISIL|Islamic State]] fighters including one woman in [[Mosul]]. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/six-islamic-state-members-including-woman-arrested-in-mosul-ministry/ (Iraqi News)]
**An [[al-Hashd al-Shaabi]] statement claims the group launched missiles over the [[Syria]]n border at [[ISIL|Islamic State]] militants preparing to launch an international assault, killing and injuring dozens of militants. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/iraqi-paramilitary-troops-repulse-islamic-state-attack-coming-from-syria/ (Iraqi News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**Thousands of pro-[[European Union]] supporters of Open Britain, the European Movement and Britain for Europe demonstrate across the [[United Kingdom]] calling for a referendum on the final terms of the UK's planned exit from the [[European Union]]. [https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/uk/thousands-of-proeu-activists-to-demonstrate-on-national-action-day-36803123.html (''The Belfast Telegraph'')]
*[[2017–18 United States political sexual scandals]]
**[[Elliott Broidy]] resigns as deputy financial chairman of the U.S. [[Republican National Committee]] following reports that he negotiated a $1.6 million payoff with a Playboy Playmate over claims he had impregnated her. [https://www.politico.com/story/2018/04/13/rnc-deputy-finance-chair-broidy-resigns-522867 (''Politico'')]
*Heads of state and government from across the Americas meet in [[Lima]], [[Peru]], for the [[8th Summit of the Americas|Eighth Summit of the Americas]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/summit-americas-begins-regional-tumult-180410122908232.html (Al Jazeera)]
*The U.S. government releases a report by Inspector General [[Michael E. Horowitz]] that accuses former FBI deputy director [[Andrew McCabe]] of improperly authorizing a media disclosure and "lack of candor" concerning this disclosure. [http://thehill.com/policy/national-security/383080-watchdog-fired-fbi-official-mccabe-leaked-to-media-to-help-himself (''The Hill'')]

;Science and technology
*Experimental satellite [[RemoveDEBRIS]] arrives at the [[International Space Station]] ahead of a planned mission removing [[orbital debris]]. [https://www.getsurrey.co.uk/news/surrey-news/space-junk-satellite-made-surrey-14510990 (GetSurrey)]
